description: MGRS grid line labels. Each case builds the grid for `bounds` at `mapWidth` px (MgrsGridRenderer.build on Android, MGRSGridRenderer.build on iOS). Every label that sits on one of the listed lines (a line is named by any MGRS point on it plus its orientation) must read `label`. Numeric labels are the line's own value: the 1 km line at northing 87000 reads 87, the 10 km line at easting 50000 reads 5. 100 km labels are the letter of the square east of a vertical line / north of a horizontal one, the same side the numbers count from. On top of the listed lines, every 1 km / 10 km label must equal the value of the line it sits on. Truncating the round-tripped UTM value used to label the 87000 line as 86 (seen on the emulator at Alcatraz).

placementDescription: Label placement (placeLabels). Each view projects with a test-only equirectangular projection about `centre`: dx = (lng - lng0) * cos(lat0) * 111320 m, dy = (lat - lat0) * 110574 m, rotated so `heading` (degrees clockwise from north) points up, then x = width/2 + dx'/metresPerPoint, y = height/2 - dy'/metresPerPoint. The grid is built for the heading-proof square around the viewport (half-diagonal radius) at mapWidth = viewport diagonal, like both map hosts. Lines running across the screen are labelled where they cross x = 0.3 * width, lines running up/down where they cross y = 0.7 * height, one label per physical line (a 100 km line shows its square letter, otherwise the 1 km value wins over the 10 km digit), nothing within 12 of the sides, 140 of the top (header) or 100 of the bottom (bottom buttons), and a column label within 16 of the row is dropped when a row label sits within 16 of the column. `column` lists the across-the-screen labels top to bottom, `row` the up/down labels left to right.
